Sales Monthly — by product category

One column-group (Sales / Cogs / Margin / Qty) per calendar month of 2026, plus Q1 and Q2 quarterly summary groups (each with that row's share of the quarter's total Sales) and an overall Total group (share of the whole window). Installment sales use Order_Status = 5 as the "real sale" filter (matches the business's own report exactly for every category+month checked); single-payment sales use Type_Of_Sales = 99 instead, keyed to Aplication_Date since they have no Order_Date. Rows are sorted by total Sales, highest first. Sales = SUM(Final_Price), Cogs = SUM(Start_Price), both raw and unmodified — same convention the business's own report uses. Snapshot pulled the same manual way as the rest of this Artifact — not live (the PHP app version refreshes from the database on every page load).

Brand Analyze — by brand

Same layout as Sales Monthly, grouped by product_brands.Brand_Name instead of product category — the Brand_ID link is fully populated in the database (unlike category), so this needed no mapping-sheet translation. Three different "no real brand" spellings found in the data (none, N/A, ბრენდის გარეშე) are combined into one "No Brand" row at the bottom. Snapshot, not live — see the Sales Monthly note above.

Subcategory Analyze — by broader product group

Same mapping-sheet lookup as Sales Monthly, just reading its Subcategory(EN) field instead of Product(EN). Snapshot, not live — see the Sales Monthly note above.

Category / Brand — brand breakdown within each category

One block per product category, brands broken down within it — same layout as the business's own reference report's "Top 4 — Brands" sheet, built here for every category found in the window instead of a hand-picked top 4. Q1/Q2 Sales are date-bounded quarterly columns; Total Sales/COGS/Margin/Qty are for the whole window (Jan 1–yesterday), matching the reference sheet's own formulas. Categories and brands within them are sorted by Total Sales, highest first (Uncategorized/No Brand always last). Snapshot, not live — see the Sales Monthly note above.

Income & Delinquency — by Product Category

Closed loans only (Close_Type IN (1, 2), keyed to Close_Date), same Jan 1–yesterday window as Sales Monthly. Income = realized (actually collected) margin, not invoiced/sale-time margin — a loan Paid Off (Close_Type=1) collected its full sale amount, one Written Off (Close_Type=2) only collected Full_Cost − Debt; that per-loan collection ratio is applied proportionally across the loan's product lines, since Cogs lives per line item but collection status lives per loan (a documented modeling simplification, not exact accounting). Delinquency = write-off rate: the share of closed loans, by quantity and by GEL, that ended up Written Off rather than Paid Off, broken down the same way (written-off GEL uses the same proportional allocation of the loan's remaining Debt). Rows sorted by Total Revenue, highest first (Uncategorized always last). Snapshot pulled the same manual way as the rest of this Artifact — not live (the PHP app version refreshes from the database on every page load).

Logistics Daily — PO & Order Fulfillment

Source: Google Sheet "Volta Order Managment". History through 20 Aug is carried over unchanged from the business's own tracking sheet; the 21 Aug column is freshly computed from the same raw data.

Sales – Pending Status = customers not yet contacted, by how long the case has been open (measured from the same Status/date basis as the sheet itself). Only "Up to 1 day" has ever had data in the source; "1 to 5 days" / ">5 days" are blank for every date shown, transferred unchanged. History through 21 Aug is from the Google Sheet as before; from 22 Aug onward, "Up to 1 day" switches source to a live daily count of instalments.Order_Status = 4 ("Pending" loan applications, a different underlying process that happens to have landed on similar numbers) captured once a day by a server cron job — not backfillable for any date that wasn't actually captured that day, same as everywhere else on this tab.

Source: Google Sheet "Volta Order Managment" (შეკვეთები / "orders" sheet). History through 20 Aug is carried over unchanged from the business's own tracking sheet; the 21 Aug column is freshly computed from the same raw order data. "Not Delivered" / age-bucket / "On Hold" figures are a snapshot valid only for the date in that column; "Delivered" and "Average Delivery Time" are reconstructed from each order's actual Delivery/Pickup Date, so those two are reliable history, not snapshots.

Not Delivered = orders not yet in "Delivered" or "Cancelled" status. Age buckets (≤1 day / 1–5 days / >5 days) are measured from each order's Sale Date, for not-yet-delivered, not-on-hold orders. Average Delivery Time = average(Delivery Date − Pickup Date) in days, only over orders where both dates are recorded — Pickup Date is sparsely filled in the source sheet, so several columns show a dash. This tab is a manual snapshot, not live; automatic daily refresh (planned for 20:00 every day) is not yet set up — it needs a Google Sheets API service account and a scheduled job on the server.

Reported Income (from Comment)

From customers.Comment — not a free-text note field despite the name, this is where staff record reported income (e.g. "1500", "1200 ლარი თიბისი ბანკში", "დღეში 100 ლ"). Bucketed by the first number found in the text; daily-wage phrasing ("დღეში" = "per day") is not converted to a monthly figure, so a handful of daily amounts sit in the same buckets as monthly ones.

Tbilisi District (decoded from address)

From customers.FactAddress, scoped to addresses mentioning "თბილისი". Real addresses don't follow one consistent format, so this is a best-effort substring match against a list of known Tbilisi districts/microrayons; the rest are "ვერ დადგინდა" (could not be determined) rather than guessed at.

Ex Customers — payment-quality grade & contact list

An "ex customer" = a Customer_ID with at least one genuinely closed loan (Close_Type IN (1, 2)) and no currently active one — 3,210 as of this build. Grade (A–E) = how much of what they bought actually got collected, weighted across all their closed loans (SUM(Full_Cost − Debt) / SUM(Full_Cost)): A ≥98% collected (paid in full) · B 80–98% · C 50–80% · D 1–50% · E <1% (collected essentially nothing). Bands were chosen by looking at the real distribution before picking round numbers — not arbitrary. Contains real customer PII (name, national ID, phone, email) — this is the one individual-row report in this project, built for collections/win-back outreach specifically because it was asked for; every other tab stays aggregate-only on purpose. Snapshot, not live — see the Sales Monthly note above.

Reconciling against Customer Analysis: Total Customers − Active Customers = ~29,768 "not currently a customer," not 3,210. The gap (~26,558) never actually received a loan in the first place — every application they ever submitted was rejected, refused, or expired before disbursement, so there's no payment history to grade. Shown below as an aggregate-only breakdown by their most recent application status (no PII), not folded into the graded list.

Never Became a Customer — by last application status (no PII)

The other ~26,500 inactive people, bucketed by whichever Order_Status their most recent application ended on. Reconciles: 3,210 (graded) + this table's total = ~29,768 = Customer Analysis's Total − Active.

Risk Segmentation — active portfolio

Active loans (Active = 1) grouped by Risk_Status. Snapshot, refreshed the same manual way as the rest of this Artifact.

Closed Loans Analysis — paid off vs. written off

One row per month, keyed to Close_Date. Only loans that were genuinely active and then closed (Close_Type 1 = paid off, 2 = written off) — excludes rejected/never-activated applications, which sit at Close_Type = 0 along with currently-active loans and aren't a real "closure." Paid Off Amount = Full_Cost (the loan's full sale price); Written Off Debt = remaining Debt at closure. Snapshot, refreshed the same manual way as the rest of this Artifact.

Overdue Analysis — Portfolio at Risk

Active loans (Active = 1) grouped by Days_Age — the reliably-populated aging field (OverDay is 0 for every active loan in this database and isn't usable). PAR30/60/90 = share of total outstanding debt that is 30/60/90+ days overdue, the standard lending "Portfolio at Risk" metric. Point-in-time snapshot — not reconstructable for a past date, same as the Logistics Daily "Not Delivered" table.

Leads — status by month

Every lead status by month, keyed to instalments.Lead_Create_Date — the same admin-panel Status filter shown in the "Leads" panel. Uses instalments.Lead_Status_ID rather than the standalone leads table: the standalone table is just the untriaged intake log (92% blank/Pending in this window), while a lead's status only actually gets updated once it's pulled into instalments (as a Lead = 1 row) and worked. "Unspecified" covers a small number of rows with no status set. Snapshot, not live — see the Sales Monthly note above.

Application Statuses — all statuses by month

Every instalments.Order_Status an application has ever carried, one row per month, keyed to Aplication_Date — the same admin-panel Status filter shown in the "Applications" panel, but covering the full status lifecycle rather than just the 5 committee outcomes on the Committee tab. Two raw codes that share the literal label "ინვოისის გაგზავნა" (IDs 5 and 9 — 5 is the one actually used at volume) are merged into one row; "Unspecified" covers a small number of rows whose status code has no label in order_statuses at all. Snapshot, not live — see the Sales Monthly note above.

Committee — decision reasons by status

There's no separate committee/reasons table — every status below is instalments.Order_Status, and every reason is instalments.Reason, the same admin-panel Status filter shown in the loan-management panel (Approved/Rejected/"Client Refused"/Expired/Not Responded). Each table is one row per month, keyed to Aplication_Date, "Unspecified" = Reason left blank, shown as its own row rather than dropped. English column is a hand-translated label for the free-text Georgian Reason (no English field exists in the database). Snapshot data (see the PHP app for the live version).

Rejected — Order_Status = 6 ("უარი განაცხადზე")

Client Refused — Order_Status = 12 ("კლიენტის უარი განაცხადზე")

Expired — Order_Status = 13

Not Responding — Order_Status = 14 ("არ პასუხობს")

Approved — Order_Status = 5 ("ინვოისის გაგზავნა", the same status used elsewhere in this project as the "real sale" filter)

Unlike the four outcomes above, an approved/sold application doesn't need a reason recorded — 11,360 of 11,361 Order_Status = 5 rows have a blank Reason (shown below almost entirely as "Unspecified"). Kept for completeness/transparency rather than hidden.
